title: Open-plan Office Lighting Design

pages.title: Design basis and office arrangement
paragraphs: This project considers the lighting of an open-plan office used for reading, paperwork and computer work. A maintained average illuminance of 500 lx is required on each desk, with a uniformity of at least 0.60 and a maximum UGR of 19 [1]. The aim is to provide enough light for these activities without large differences across the working area or excessive glare from the fittings.

The office is L-shaped and extends around the central service core. The area enclosed by the traced internal wall boundaries is 1042.10 m2. Deducting the parts occupied by the eight columns gives 1032.57 m2. This differs from the 1022 m2 annotation on the drawing. The traced boundary defines the model and the 1042.10 m2 internal floor area used for BEC calculations.

The supplied drawing does not show office furniture, so 28 four-person bench groups have been arranged within the space. This gives 112 desks, each 1.6 by 0.8 m. Their positions provide a basis for checking the lighting where people would be working. The calculation assumes this furniture arrangement and would need to be reviewed if the desks were moved significantly.

A ceiling height of 2.8 m and a desk height of 0.8 m are adopted. Ceiling, wall and floor reflectances are assumed to be 80%, 70% and 20%, respectively, with 40% for the columns. The relatively light ceiling and walls help distribute reflected light through the office. These finishes would need to be maintained in the completed space, since darker surfaces would change the calculated lighting performance. Daylight is not included because the glazing dimensions are unavailable.

pages.title: DIALux model and calculation procedure
paragraphs: The architectural drawing was imported into DIALux evo and checked against the 45 m overall dimension. The office boundary and eight full-height columns were modelled so that their obstruction of light is included.

The manufacturer ULD file provides the light distribution used in the calculation [2]. DIALux accounts for reflected light using the surface reflectances in Table 1. The fittings occupy complete 600 mm ceiling tiles, with their emitting faces approximately level with the 2.8 m ceiling. The native report lists the luminaire reference position at 2.868 m, 68 mm above the adopted ceiling plane. Figure 1 shows the model and evaluation heights.

Each 1.6 by 0.8 m desk has a 10 by 5 calculation grid at 0.8 m. Under EN 12464-1 clause 5.4, a 2:1 area uses its short side, so the maximum spacing is 0.2 x 5^log10(0.8) = 0.171 m [1]. The 0.16 m grid meets this limit. DIALux reports Uo as minimum divided by mean illuminance [3]. Checking desks individually exposes local shortfalls that a room mean would hide.

A maintenance factor of 0.80 was applied to allow for the reduction in illumination during use [4]. Glare was calculated at a seated eye height of 1.2 m, with viewing directions at 15-degree intervals [5]. The manufacturer lists a catalogue UGR value for the fitting, but the glare experienced in the office also depends on its position and surroundings. The calculated room values are therefore used for the comparison with the UGR limit.

Further calculations were made for the 0.5 m bands around the bench groups, the remaining background floor, cylindrical illuminance at seated head height, and the exposed walls and ceiling. These use the same fittings and positions as the desk calculation. The desks are calculation surfaces; solid furniture, monitor screens and high partitions are not included. Separate copies were used for the output and reflectance comparisons, with all other inputs held constant.

pages.title: Luminaire selection and layout
paragraphs: The selected fitting is the Philips PowerBalance gen2 RC461B 40S/840, order code 910505103638. The design uses 186 fittings, each rated at 4000 lm and 23 W (174 lm/W). A colour temperature of 4000 K and a colour rendering index above 80 are appropriate for the office activities considered here [2]. The catalogue UGR 16 optic was also an important consideration because occupants will be using computer screens as well as reading printed material.

The 597 by 597 mm fitting fits within a 600 mm ceiling tile. Following the grid avoids fittings crossing tile joints. Spacing is generally about 2.4 m, with adjustments near columns and room edges. Figure 3 shows the layout and the two principal photometric planes. Their similar downward distributions support overlapping light at desk height. The curves help explain the choice of optic; the actual spacing and glare are assessed using the room calculation.

Keeping the same 186 positions, the 3400 lm version achieved a minimum desk mean of 504 lx. The 4000 lm version raised it to 593 lx, with the maximum directional UGR still below 19. This gives more margin for darker finishes and output reduction.
Allow at least 86 mm for the fitting body, plus driver and maintenance clearance [2]. Drawing L01 on page 10 identifies each fitting and gives the luminaire schedule.

pages.title: Calculated performance and code comparison
paragraphs: All 112 desks meet the selected illuminance, uniformity and glare criteria. The lowest desk average is 593 lx, the lowest uniformity is 0.80 and the highest calculated UGR is 18.1. These values occur at different desks. Figure 4 shows the variation in desk-average illuminance across the office, with the three desks giving the limiting results identified.

Desk-021 averages 593 lx at the south perimeter. Its centre is 2.40 m from the boundary; L140 and L136 are about 1.0 and 1.4 m away, bracketing the desk north to south. The perimeter limits additional coverage from rows farther south. L013 is about 7.7 m away.

pages.title: Lighting controls and energy use
paragraphs: The office has 32 independent control zones: 28 for bench groups and four for circulation. Each has local manual switching and dimming. The largest zone is 46.67 m2, below the 250 m2 automatic-control limit. The 1042.10 m2 office requires 32 manual control points under BEC Table 5.5 without claiming a reduction for low power density [6]. Figure 5 shows their boundaries.

Each zone switches off after 10 minutes without occupancy, within the BEC limit of 15 minutes. A schedule switches lighting off outside working hours, with local overrides limited to 120 minutes. Commissioning must confirm at least 50% power reduction, including sensor and driver standby consumption [6, Sec. 5.6.1].

Daylight-responsive control is proposed where the actual external glazing and lighting load trigger BEC clause 5.6.2 [6]. The window dimensions and grouping are needed to define these zones and check the exceptions. Where applicable, the controller must be able to reduce lighting power to 50% or less, or switch off, in response to daylight.

The fittings draw 186 x 23 = 4278 W. With a provisional 50 W allowance for sensors and shared control equipment, the design load is 4328 W, or 4.153 W/m2 over 1042.10 m2. The BEC limit is 7.2 W/m2. A full-load scenario of 2500 h/year gives approximately 10.82 MWh/year. A controlled estimate requires logged occupancy, driver power at dimmed output and standby loads.

pages.title: Design comparison and conclusion
paragraphs: DIALux tested 90% output, lower ceiling/wall/floor reflectances (70/50/20%), and both together. The layout and MF were retained. Table 4 shows the workstation results.

At 90% output, the lowest desk mean is 534 lx, 6.8% above the target. The worst directional UGR falls from 18.1 to 17.7. Lower reflectance at full output reduces the minimum desk mean to 566 lx while the UGR rises to 18.6, leaving 0.4 below the limit.

With both changes, the lowest desk mean is 509 lx and maximum directional UGR is 18.2. The 9 lx illuminance margin supports keeping full output as the design setting and tuning the installed system after completion.

The maintenance factor uses LLMF x LSF x LMF x RSMF = 0.90 x 1.00 x 0.95 x 0.94 = 0.8037, rounded down to 0.80 [4]. The product declares L90 at 50,000 h [2]. The remaining factors assume prompt replacement, annual cleaning and retained room finishes.

Full output remains the design setting. The 593 lx minimum maintained desk mean is 19% above 500 lx and corresponds to about 741 lx initially under the adopted MF. Local dimming can be commissioned against the installed finishes, desks and screens. Actual dimmed power should be verified separately.
pages.0: Two further DIALux calculations were made with the same layout and maintenance factor. One reduced all luminaire outputs to 90%. The other retained full output and changed ceiling/wall/floor reflectances from 80/70/20% to 70/50/20%. Table 4 shows the workstation results; Appendix C gives the auxiliary results and selected outputs.

appendix: All three comparison cases meet the adopted auxiliary criteria. The combined case gives the lowest seated cylindrical mean (180 lx) and ceiling mean (111 lx). Appendix C compares these surfaces; Table 4 gives the workstation results.

The combined case retains only 9 lx above the 500 lx desk requirement. Full output is the design basis. The 4328 W full-load budget includes the provisional control allowance. Actual electrical savings require driver power data and operating hours.

critical_desks: Desk-084 has the lowest Uo (0.80), with a range of 521-736 lx around a 654 lx mean. L120 is only 0.36 m from the desk centre and sits toward one side of the desk. The native isolux plot shows a gradient across the task area, consistent with uneven overlap from the adjacent fittings.

At Desk-018 the highest directional UGR is 18.1 at 180 degrees. Several luminaires are close to the observer, with L028 and L014 within 1.5 m in plan. The directional result reflects the combined effect of source luminance, apparent position and background luminance. The export gives the total, so individual source contributions remain unquantified.
